newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares hold gains on strong dollar, Wall St.
newsitem.headline: German shares hold gains on strong dollar, Wall St.

text.p: German shares held most of their gains over the course of Wednesday afternoon, ending off earlier highs but supported by the unstoppable dollar and bullish news from Wall Street, where the Dow breached 8,000 points for the first time.
The IBIS DAX index ended at 4,223.69 points, up 84.01 points or 2.03 percent, off earlier highs at 4,234.87 points.
Its counterpart in bourse trade, the DAX index, ended earlier at 4,201.24 points, up 1.94 percent or 80.11 points, having broken through 4,200 points over the session.

"Dealers here are just as surprised as everyone else about the continued rise of the market. The environment is right, even though everyone is still waiting for the long-overdue correction," a Frankfurt trader said.
Generally it was a good day for breaking psychological barriers, as the Dow Jones Industrial index also broke 8,000 points for the first time, before falling back after Eastman Kodak Co opened lower.
Underpinning the strength of the DAX was still the U.S. dollar, which traded near 1.80 marks all afternoon.
Among shares on the move was Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, which ended up 4,30 marks, or 5.49 percent, at 82.60 marks.
"There are no special reasons for this. A lot of it is probably down to the usual takeover speculation," said the trader.
The volume leaders in the afternoon were the banks and the chemical stocks, which traders attributed to positive sentiment in both sectors.
BASF AG led volumes, up 2.45 marks at 71.35 marks, while Bayer AG ended up 1.23 marks at 75.73 marks and Hoechst AG ended up 3.53 marks at 85.63.
Deutsche Bank AG closed the day up 1.15 marks at 107.90 marks, Commerzbank AG up 1.41 marks at 53.76 marks, while Dresdner was up 3.79 marks at 75.19 marks.
"There were good volumes across the board which helped all the major stocks, not just banks and chemicals, even if they were particularly favoured," a trader said.

Retailer Karstadt AG was one of the days top gainers. It closed up 47.40 marks, or 7.39 percent, at 688.50 marks, boosted by expectations that restructuring at the group would soon take hold, despite expectations that it could be dropped from the DAX in favour of Adidas AG.
